notes.meaning: King Lemuel records the wise instruction that his mother taught him. An earthly ruler receives godly wisdom directly from his mother, showing how much spiritual influence a faithful parent can have. Her words carry the weight of an inspired message from God.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars see Lemuel as an unknown king from the Arabian region of Massa rather than an alternate name for King Solomon.

notes.meaning: Lemuel's mother repeats her tender call three times to grab his full attention. She reminds him that he was born from her own body and given by God in answer to her prayers and vows. Because she has invested so much prayer and love into his life, she urges him to take her warnings seriously.

A king is warned not to spend his strength and vitality chasing after many women. Giving oneself over to uncontrolled sexual desires drains a man's health, fortune, and mental focus. Throughout history, foolish passions have brought about the downfall of powerful rulers.

Kings and princes are warned against drinking wine and craving strong drink. Intoxicating drink clouds the mind and leads rulers to forget God's laws. A king who is drunk cannot judge fairly and will end up crushing the rights of the poor and oppressed.

differ.view: Some teach that this passage commands total abstinence from all alcoholic drinks for leaders and believers alike.
Many teach that the passage forbids drunkenness and excess that impair judgment, while allowing moderate drinking.

notes.meaning: Strong drink and wine belong to the dying and those trapped in bitter grief, not to ruling kings. In ancient times, wine served as a medicine and painkiller to ease the suffering of the desperately sick and faint. It brings temporary relief to people enduring agonizing physical or mental sorrow.

differ.view: Read with verse 4, this verse limits wine to those who are 'ready to perish' and to no one else.

notes.meaning: The king is commanded to speak up for people who have no voice in a court of law. He must step in to defend poor, fatherless, and frightened citizens who cannot plead their own cases. God calls rulers to judge with complete honesty and protect those whom society leaves behind.

A poem in alphabetical order begins by asking who can find an excellent and capable wife. A woman of such rare moral strength and godly character is worth far more than precious jewels. A wise person values inner character above wealth or physical charm.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view this acrostic poem as a poetic hymn to personified Lady Wisdom rather than a profile of an individual housewife.

notes.meaning: Her husband places his complete trust in her because she manages their household with great integrity and skill. Because she is so dependable, he never lacks any valuable gain. Throughout the entire course of her life, she consistently seeks his good and never causes him harm.

She gathers raw materials like wool and flax to make clothing for her household. She does not wait for others to force her into duty, but works willingly and joyfully with her hands. Even as a woman of rank, she sets a bright example of productive labor.

Like merchant ships trading across distant seas, she brings fine provisions into her home from far away. She uses creativity and enterprise to trade her own goods for choice food and supplies. Her energetic care ensures her household enjoys variety and plenty.

She wakes up while it is still dark to prepare food for her family and assign daily tasks to her servant girls. She puts the needs of others ahead of her own personal comfort and sleep. Her daily routine begins with orderly planning so the whole house runs smoothly.

She carefully examines a field and buys it with money she has earned through her own hard work. She turns that land into an asset by planting a fruitful vineyard. Her sharp business mind helps build long-term security for her family.

She tucks in her robes and sets herself to work with energetic determination. By taking on useful labor and daily exercise, she keeps her body and mind strong and active. She approaches hard work with courage rather than laziness.

She discovers through experience that her business ventures and trade goods are successful. Her lamp stays lit late into the night, showing her watchful care over the home and her ongoing industry. Her hard work brings real satisfaction and steady profit.

She takes up the distaff and spindle, the ancient tools used to spin raw wool into yarn. Even though she oversees a large and wealthy estate, she does not look down on manual labor. Her personal diligence sets a standard of skill for everyone around her.

She opens her hands wide to give generously to the poor and afflicted. Her hard work is not meant just to build personal wealth, but to provide resources she can share with people in need. True godliness always shows itself in practical charity.

When freezing cold weather and winter snow arrive, she has no fear for her household. She has planned ahead and made sure all her family members are dressed in thick, warm, scarlet clothing. Wise foresight keeps her home protected from sudden hardships.

She makes beautiful tapestries and coverings to furnish her home in comfort and dignity. She dresses herself in fine linen and rich purple cloth, clothing suited to her high character and social standing. Her home reflects order, beauty, and proper care.

Her husband is well known and respected at the city gates, where the elders and judges meet to govern the community. Her excellent management of the estate frees him from domestic worries so he can serve the public. A godly spouse helps build her partner's good name.

She makes fine linen clothing and crafts ornamental sashes, selling them to traveling merchants. Her home manufacturing is of such high quality that outside traders readily buy her products. She uses her talents to support her family and bless the wider community.

Spiritual strength and personal honor are her real clothing, shaping how she carries herself each day. Because she has planned faithfully and trusts God's care, she can smile at the future without fear. Real security comes from a life grounded in godly wisdom.

Whenever she speaks, her words are filled with practical wisdom and godly instruction. The law of kindness directs her tongue, so she corrects and guides others with gentle patience instead of harsh anger. Her speech builds up everyone who hears her.

She watches carefully over everything that goes on in her house, guiding her children and servants with wisdom. She refuses to sit around being lazy or eat food she has not worked to provide. Faithful oversight brings peace, order, and safety to the home.

Her children stand up to honor her and declare how blessed they are to have her, while her husband praises her with deep love. He tells her that although many women have done noble and valiant deeds, she surpasses every one of them. A life of quiet faithfulness earns the deepest gratitude from those closest to home.

Outward charm can be dishonest, and physical beauty fades quickly with passing years. A woman whose life is shaped by reverence and faith in the Lord has a beauty that lasts forever. Fearing God is the true foundation of an honorable life.

She deserves to enjoy the full reward of what her hands have earned through patient labor. Even if people fail to compliment her, the lasting results of her good works will openly praise her in public gatherings. God ensures that quiet, loving service will be honored in the end.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Early Church teachers like Gregory the Great read the gates spiritually as the day of judgment and the gates of heaven, where holy deeds will receive their eternal praise.
